Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus Energy Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. If you would like to register for a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Nexus Energy Corp.'s Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are John Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Steve Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Mark Ellis, Chief Strategy Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1. Outstanding generation fleet performance and availability.
    2. Progress towards clean energy goals and emission reductions.
    3. Key achievements and challenges during the quarter.
    4. Updates on regulatory rate case filings and outcomes.
    5. Disciplined dividend policy and payout ratio strategy.
    6. Strong comparison of current period results to prior periods and guidance.

Let me provide some more detail on these six key aspects.

First, on our generation fleet performance and availability. Our fleet, totaling 28 GW of nameplate capacity across 45 major facilities, delivered another quarter of strong results, underscoring the resilience of our diversified portfolio amid volatile weather patterns, supply chain headwinds, and accelerating decarbonization pressures. For the quarter, our fleet-wide equivalent availability factor came in at 92.8%, up 150 basis points year-over-year and exceeding our internal target of 91.5%. This marks our sixth straight quarter above 92%, reflecting the payoff from our $450 million multi-year fleet optimization program launched in 2022. Capacity factor across the board averaged 68.4%, a 3.2 percentage point improvement from Q3 2023, driven by higher renewable dispatch and thermal baseload stability. Total net generation hit 52.4 TWh, up 7% quarter-over-quarter, with adjusted EBITDA contribution from generation assets rising 12% to $1.2 billion.

Breaking it down by asset class, our thermal fleet—primarily combined-cycle gas turbines and a legacy coal portfolio comprising 14 GW—posted an EAF of 93.2%, with forced outage rates at just 1.8%, down from 2.4% last year. Heat rates improved to 7,420 BTU/kWh on average, a 2.1% gain, thanks to our adoption of GE's Advanced Gas Path upgrades on six H-class units at our Mid-Atlantic hubs. This boosted efficiency and reduced CO2 emissions intensity by 4% quarter-over-quarter. Our Ravenswood CCGT in New York ran at a 78% capacity factor, capitalizing on PJM's tight capacity auction dynamics, where we cleared 95% of our offered capacity at $250/MW-day.

Coal assets, now just 12% of our thermal mix following 2021 retirements, maintained solid availability at 91.5% EAF, despite elevated O&M costs from reagent pricing up 15% due to limestone supply constraints. We're on track to retire our final two units at the Cumberland plant by Q4 2025, in line with MATS compliance and regional air quality mandates, with repowering options under evaluation using iron-air batteries for long-duration storage.

Our nuclear fleet of 4.2 GW, anchored by three uprated AP1000 reactors at Seabrook and Limerick, achieved a stellar 93.1% capacity factor and 95.2% EAF, our best in five years. Unplanned outages totaled only 48 hours fleet-wide, versus the industry average of 120 hours per EPRI benchmarks. This generated 9.8 TWh, supporting 18% of New England's winter peak demand. Key enabler was our rollout of Framatome's GAIA digital twin platform, using AI-driven predictive analytics to cut refueling outage durations by 15%—we shaved two days off Limerick's Cycle 16 outage in July.

Renewables contributed 42% of our output at 22.1 TWh. Wind assets, 8.5 GW primarily in ERCOT and MISO, delivered a 42.3% capacity factor, boosted by favorable Gulf wind regimes and our 200 MW repower at the Lone Star Wind Farm with Vestas V150-4.2 MW turbines. Solar PV, 6.2 GW concentrated in SPP and CAISO, hit 28.7% CF, up from 25.9% last year, aided by First Solar's thin-film Series 7 modules that outperformed in dusty Southwest conditions. Hybrid solar-plus-storage projects, like our 300 MW/1,200 MWh facility in Arizona with Tesla Megapacks, achieved 98% inverter availability, mitigating duck curve challenges and unlocking $45 million in ancillary services revenue from CAISO's resource adequacy markets.

Regionally, PJM and NYISO, 35% of fleet, saw 93.5% EAF, with gas and nuclear offsetting coal phase-outs amid 15% higher heating degree days. ERCOT, 25% exposure, had wind and gas at 91.8% EAF, navigating URMP-driven retirements—our fleet avoided curtailments during August's heat dome. MISO and SPP, 30%, benefited from wind tails at 92.1% EAF, though Midwest coal faced 3% higher forced outages from coal quality issues. Out West in WECC, solar and hydro, our 1.8 GW portfolio, averaged 89.4% EAF, tempered by Colorado River drought but offset by our 150 MW pumped storage expansion at Cabin Creek.

Challenges included hurricane season impacting Gulf Coast gas units with 72 hours of precautionary shutdowns, contributing 0.4% to FOR. Reagent and turbine blade supply chains remain pressured—Siemens Energy delays pushed two maintenance windows into Q4. Cyber threats loomed, but we had zero reportable incidents thanks to our ISO 27001-certified SOC and Dragos partnerships for OT cybersecurity.

Strategically, our $1.2 billion 2024-2026 capex includes $300 million for hydrogen-readiness at five CCGT sites, blending up to 20% green H2 by 2027 per DOE's HyBlend program—early tests at our Texas Gateway plant hit 95% combustion stability. Battery integration is ramping: 1.5 GWh added YTD, targeting 5 GWh by 2026 to firm renewables and arbitrage ERCOT's negative pricing events, 120 hours this summer. We're piloting GE Vernova's fleet-wide Asset Performance Management software, forecasting a 1-2% EAF uplift and $50 million annual O&M savings.

Looking ahead, Q4 EAF guidance is 92.5-93.5%, with full-year capacity factor at 68-69%. Risks include El Niño-driven hydro variability and FERC Order 2222 delays, but tailwinds from IRA Section 45X PTC adders—$120/MWh for advanced nuclear—and rising capacity payments position us well. Our EAF outperforms Duke Energy's 91.2% and NextEra's renewables benchmark of 40% CF, affirming top-quartile status per S&P Global.

Moving to our second aspect, progress towards clean energy goals and emission reductions. Year-to-date, we've achieved a 32% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions from our 2019 baseline of 45 million metric tons of CO2e, bringing us to 30.6 million metric tons. That's ahead of our interim 2030 target of 50% reduction, driven by the accelerated retirement of 1.8 GW of legacy coal fleet, including the full phase-out of Unit 3 at our Midwest Basin plant in Ohio, shaving off 2.2 million tons of CO2e annually. On a generation-weighted basis, carbon intensity has dropped to 320 grams CO2e per kWh, down from 480 last year, placing us in the top quartile among peers like Duke Energy and Southern Company per EPA's eGRID database.

Renewables are the engine. We've commissioned 850 MW of new capacity in Q3, including the 450 MW Solar Horizon project in ERCOT—our largest utility-scale solar farm, featuring bifacial PERC modules from LONGi at 25.8% efficiency. This brings renewables to 8.7 GW, 35% of our mix, up from 28% year-end 2023. Wind repowering at 300 MW Prairie Winds in PJM boosted capacity factors to 42%, a 15% improvement via Siemens Gamesa's 5.X-14 offshore-class turbines. We've locked 15-year PPAs with hyperscalers like Google and Microsoft for 70% of new capacity at $28/MWh blended pricing, below our sub-$20/MWh LCOE thanks to IRA PTC/ITC multipliers.

In the U.S. Southeast, serving 4 million customers across Carolinas and Georgia, renewables hit 28% penetration, fueled by 200 MW Sweetwater Solar amid data center demand from Meta's Atlanta hubs. Midwest coal retirements aligned with MISO rules unlocked $450 million in avoided fuel costs YTD; Texas assets benefited from ERCOT curtailment reforms, dispatching 95% of 1.2 GW wind. Our 15% stake in UK's Hornsea 3 offshore wind delivered first power at 42% capacity factor, positioning for £500 million REC monetization through 2030 via Contracts for Difference.

Technically, our $250 million CCS investment at the Gateway gas plant in Pennsylvania hit 90% capture rates on syngas, sequestering 1.1 million tons CO2e annually with Occidental's STRATOS hub. Green hydrogen Phase 1 at 100 MW Desert Bloom in Arizona produced 8,000 tons H2, feeding peakers for 20% NOx reductions and DOE H2Hub grants. Our 200 MW/800 MWh BESS at Texas Independence arbitraged 150 GWh YTD, enabling 25% more renewable integration and stabilizing $1.2 billion merchant revenues.

These moves de-risk amid $4/MMBtu Henry Hub gas and EPA Clean Power Plan 2.0. We've hedged 85% of 2025 gas at $3.50/MMBtu; renewables hedge EU ETS equivalents. Capex guidance $2.8-3.2 billion FY24, 60% clean tech, 12% ROIC on renewables vs. 8% gas CTs. Supply chain delays on HVDC pushed two wind projects, but 2.5 GW pipeline and Orsted JV keep us ahead. Renewables are cash flow positive, emissions trajectory downward, enhancing our A-rated profile and 5-7% EPS growth.

Third, key achievements and challenges during the quarter. We delivered a standout quarter, exceeding guidance amid robust demand and clean energy execution in CAISO, WECC, and SPP markets. Adjusted EBITDA hit $1.2 billion, up 18% year-over-year, driven by 12% generation increase to 28.5 TWh. Renewables hit 62% of mix, up from 55%; 1.2 GW new solar-plus-storage at Desert Sun and Eagle Peak came online at 98% capacity factor, with 400 MWh Tesla Megapacks securing 15-year PPAs with Google/Microsoft at $45/MWh average, above $38/MWh hedge.

Thermal CCGTs, 1,800 MW GE 7HA fleet, ran 85% capacity factor in summer peaks, supporting CAISO reliability; 'Fleet Optimization 2.0' cut O&M 7% via Siemens MindSphere, reducing outages 22%, expanding margins to 42%. Regulated utility added 45,000 residential connections, up 9% YoY from EV incentives under NEM 3.0; C&I revenues grew 14% with 200 MW semiconductor fab deal. Revenues $4.8 billion, +11% YoY, weather-normalized retail +8%.

Strategically, advanced net-zero-by-2040: retired 300 MW Wyoming coal early, replaced with 500 MW Ørsted wind, unlocking $150 million IRA ITC/Green Bank funding. Battery pipeline 3.5 GW, 1 GW construction for curtailment avoidance at 30% CAISO solar.

Challenges: gas prices spiked 25% to $4.20/MMBtu Socal, $80 million under-recovery, mitigated by 75% hedge at $3.50 through 2025. Supply chain delays on transformers/SF6-free gear deferred $50 million HVDC capex. FERC capped ROE at 9.2% vs. 9.5% target, trimming EPS $0.08; AB 205 battery costs $20 million, wildfire capex +15% to $300 million. Atmospheric river curtailed 1.2 TWh hydro 5%; WECC congestion $30 million. Debt expense +$40 million at 4.8% yield, offset by $500 million prepay saving $15 million/year.

These highlight leadership—renewables 40% EBITDA—while demanding hedging. Raising FY EBITDA to $4.6-4.8 billion, 15% growth.

Fourth, updates on regulatory rate case filings and outcomes. We made meaningful progress across dockets, securing over $450 million incremental annual revenue YTD, 92% capture vs. EEI 75-80% average. Focus aligns $12.5 billion five-year capex with resiliency, decarbonization, affordability amid 4.2% YoY customer usage growth from Ohio manufacturing, Michigan EVs. We operate 15,000 MW across thermal/nuclear/renewables/storage, serving 4.2 million in Ohio/Michigan/Indiana/Pennsylvania under PUCO/MPSC/IURC/PPUC, MISO/PJM wholesale.

Ohio PUCO: $620 million filing on $4.2 billion rate base concluded September; requested 10.25% ROE/52% equity, got 9.75%/50%, $512 million (83% ask). Full recovery $1.2 billion Buckeye Solar-storage, renewable rider, MYRP for $300 million substations/1.2 GW offshore. Boosts Ohio EPS 15 cents, 6.5% rate base CAGR to 2028; outperforms AEP Ohio's 9.4%.

Michigan MPSC U-20878: $380 million amended, 100% Clean Energy Rider for 450 MW community solar/$150 million ThumbLoop; 9.9% ROE +50 bps incentive, $295 million (92%), SFV tariff shifts 55% residential to fixed.

Indiana IURC 45745: $250 million progressing, interim $180 million QIP for smart meters (85% penetration); expect $220-230 million Q4 for 150 MW storage.

Pennsylvania PPUC: $420 million August filing, PBR pilot tying 20% revenues to SAIDI/SAIFI via AI vegetation mgmt; 85-90% settlement likelihood for 500 MW data PPAs.

Trends: trackers cover 35% capex vs. 22% prior, avg ROE 9.8% > S&P peers. Decarb wins: CCUS on coal (90% Mitsubishi), H2 pilots, $500 million PTC/ITC. Midwest thawing on hikes with 7% industrial growth; Northeast caps CPI+1%. Outpace ComEd's 9.2% ROE via 98% capex in-service. FERC MISO transmission Q1 2025 for $2 billion Tranche 3. Supports 5-7% 2025 EPS, 7.2% rate base.

Fifth, our dividend policy and payout ratio strategy, a cornerstone of shareholder returns. We've paid dividends uninterrupted for 68 years, Dividend Aristocrat like Duke/Southern. Policy: sustainable growth while keeping A-/A3 ratings, funding capex for transition/load growth. Past five years, 5.2% CAGR vs. S&P Utilities 4.1%; today 6% hike to $0.78 quarterly, 4.2% yield vs. 4.3% 10-year Treasury—15th annual increase from regulated growth/unregulated margins.

Target 65-75% adjusted GAAP earnings payout, achieved decade-long incl. Uri/Duck Curve; 2023 71%, $2.1 billion OCF/$1.8 billion FCF. YTD Q2 68%, $1.42 EPS/$0.97 annualized. Predictable from PPAs/tolling/9.8% ROEs in eight states.

Metrics: Earnings 65-75%; FFO 75-80% (2023 73%); DCF 1.7-2.0x like NextEra. Weathered 8% O&M inflation, $1.2 billion dividends/$3.5 billion capex.

Supports: 40% capex to 2.5 GW solar-storage CAISO/ERCOT by 2026, IRA 12% yield, 500 MW Victory Solar 90% contracted; $800 million nuclear uprates 10% to 2.4 GW PJM for $100+/MWh hyperscaler PPAs; $1.5 billion T&D PJM 2.5% load, ERCOT 15% peaker margins post-Uri.

Reaffirm 2024 68-72%, 6-8% EPS growth, 1.8x+ coverage; long-term 5%+ growth from 7% rate base to $45 billion/10%+ ROIC. $400 million buybacks below 14x P/E.

Sixth, comparison of current results to prior periods and guidance. Revenues $2.85 billion Q3 2024, +12% YoY from $2.54 billion Q3 2023, +8% seq from $2.64 billion Q2. Driven by 15% YoY power sales from data centers ERCOT/CAISO, 20% above forecasts. Regulated steady despite -10% HDDS, +5% EV.

Adjusted EBITDA $785 million, +18% YoY from $665 million, +11% seq $705 million; margins 27.5% from 26.2%. Gas $2.85/MMBtu -15% YoY aided CCGTs Diablo Canyon 2.5 GW; renewables 28% mix +6 pts, 450 MW solar-storage Mojave/Central Valley PPAs Meta/Google. Offset 300 MW MISO coal retire, remarketed 80% battery-hybrid.

Regulated $1.6 billion rev +9% YoY, 10.2% ROE; $650 million capex grid hardening/microgrids 15 GW data load. Unregulated $1.25 billion +17%, 35% margins $250/MWh ERCOT; nuclear Palisades 1.1 GW 95% CF +$120 million.

Net income $420 million, $0.85 adj EPS beat consensus $0.07 vs. $0.72 Q3'23/$0.78 Q2. FCF $550 million pre-growth capex supports $0.42 div/$300 million repurchases. Leverage 3.4x.

O&M +7% to $420 million labor/transformers; hedge slippage PJM $20 million. ERCOT peaks 85 GW, CAISO duck +12% arbitraged $15 million ancillaries.

Guidance: FY24 adj EBITDA $3.15-3.25 billion up from $3.05-3.20B, 14% growth; EPS $3.40-3.50 from $3.30-3.50. Capex $4.2-4.4B 60% clean: 1 GW solar/wind/800 MW storage/100 MW H2 Diablo/Plug. 2025 initial $3.45-3.65B EBITDA +12%, EPS $3.75-3.95. Drivers: 2 GW renewables Amazon/Microsoft 1.5 GW $45-55/MWh, rate base $45B. Data centers +25 TWh/8% load.

Pillars: retire 1.5 GW coal 2026 70/30 hybrids; $2B CCUS 45Q; VPPs 500 MW Tesla. Risks NEM 3.0/FERC PJM, 85% hedge floor.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Steve Harlan to discuss the financials.

Steve Harlan: Thank you, John. Good morning, everyone. For the Q3 2024, we reported earnings per share of $1.05 and revenue of $2.85 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $850 million, primarily focused on renewables expansion, nuclear life extensions, and grid resilience upgrades. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate mid-single-digit EPS growth for 2025, with adjusted EBITDA of $3.2 to $3.4 billion.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Steve. Let me provide an update on the operational front. We are seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas turbine power plants due to the implementation of AI-driven predictive maintenance systems. This has resulted in a 15% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 25%.

Mark Ellis: Thank you, Lisa. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the long-duration energy storage space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the ERCOT and PJM markets.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Mark. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed Dragos Platform for OT cybersecurity to enhance our defenses against cyber threats.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Steve, Lisa, Mark, and Elena. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: If you would like to ask a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for dividend growth and payout strategy going forward?

John Ramirez: Certainly, Ben. As John outlined earlier, our disciplined approach targets 65-75% payout with multi-metric coverage, supporting 5%+ annual growth funded by rate base expansion and strong ROIC. We're confident in maintaining this trajectory.

Operator: Our next question comes from Alicia Rivera with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alicia Rivera: What is your outlook for regulatory outcomes in key states next year?

Steve Harlan: Thanks, Alicia. With our strong track record—92% capture YTD—and proactive filings like the Pennsylvania PBR pilot, we expect continued favorable resolutions supporting 7%+ rate base growth, aligning with capex needs.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Tom Lee: How are you mitigating risks related to supply chain issues in fleet maintenance?

Lisa Chen: Good question, Tom. We've diversified suppliers, accelerated domestic sourcing for transformers, and leveraged digital twins for predictive planning, keeping FOR low and EAF above 92%.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to John Ramirez for closing remarks.

John Ramirez: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Nexus Energy Corp. for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Nexus Energy Corp.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
